moduleTitle: Assigning and completing work for Business Architects
learningObjectives: Describe the business value of Pega's workflow automation features associated with routing and approvals.
Explain the importance of work groups in improving process efficiency.
Differentiate between the goal and deadline intervals relative to Service-Level Agreements.
Explain how Case Urgency functions in guaranteeing timely work completion.

elements.description: Routing sends each Assignment to the best-available user so work reaches the right person/team at the right time. It orchestrates workflow across functional teams and improves operational efficiency and customer experience.

items: WORKLIST — Assignments routed to a SPECIFIC user (operator) to work individually
WORK QUEUE — a SHARED queue for a team/Work Group; any qualified member can pull and complete the work

elements.description: In App Studio an Assignment Step can route to the current user, a specific named user, or a Work Queue. Routing decisions depend on whether work is personal or shared across a team.

elements.text: A Worklist is your personal inbox (addressed to you); a Work Queue is a shared team inbox (anyone on the team can grab the next item). Routing is the mailroom deciding which inbox each task goes to.

bulletPoints: Route to a specific user (Worklist) when one person must own the task; route to a Work Queue when any qualified team member can handle it.
Business-logic routing (e.g., by skill) targets the best-available user.

elements.description: A Work Group associates a set of users and Work Queues under a manager, organizing who collaborates on work. Cross-functional Work Groups bring members from different teams together to complete work that spans functions, improving process efficiency.

elements.text: A Work Group is a project team roster; a cross-functional Work Group is a task force pulled from multiple departments so the whole Case can be handled without hand-off delays.

bulletPoints: Work Groups improve efficiency by coordinating users and their shared Work Queues.
In Dev Studio terminology, a Team in App Studio corresponds to a Work Group.

elements.description: An approval routes a Case to a user to approve or reject; the outcome determines the path (approved continues the primary path; rejected branches to rework or rejection handling). Approvals are a key OOTB workflow-automation feature.

items: CASCADING — MULTIPLE approvers in sequence (e.g., up a reporting hierarchy or via an authority matrix for higher amounts)

elements.text: Single approval is one signature on the form; cascading approval is a signature chain that climbs the org chart until the amount is fully authorized.

bulletPoints: Cascading approvals can be driven by a reporting structure or an authority matrix (condition-based levels).
Approve/reject outcomes route the Case down different paths.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Managing Work Deadlines: SLAs and Urgency

elements.description: An SLA defines time targets for completing an Assignment or Case. App Studio exposes a GOAL interval and a DEADLINE interval (Dev Studio adds advanced options). In Dev Studio terms, a goal/deadline IS the Service-Level Agreement rule.
Two SLA time thresholds on an Assignment or Case:
items: GOAL — the EARLIER target; work SHOULD be completed by this time
DEADLINE — the LATER limit; work MUST be completed by this time

elements.description: A numeric priority value that ensures work is completed on time. Urgency starts at an initial value and increases automatically as the SLA's Goal and Deadline thresholds pass.

elements.text: Goal vs. deadline is a 'please reply by Friday' (goal) versus 'absolutely no later than Monday' (deadline). Urgency is the volume knob — it gets louder at the goal and louder still at the deadline so the task can't be ignored.

bulletPoints: Goal = should-finish-by (earlier); Deadline = must-finish-by (later); passing them escalates urgency.
Higher Urgency = higher priority, so overdue/at-risk work rises to the top of the list.
Advanced SLA behavior (initial urgency, business-day handling, extra escalations) is configured by SAs in Dev Studio.

examPitfalls.title: Worklist vs. Work Queue
examPitfalls.trapDescription: These are routinely swapped. Worklist = one specific user; Work Queue = shared team queue.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: One owner → Worklist (route to a specific user). Any qualified team member → Work Queue.

examPitfalls.title: Goal vs. Deadline direction
examPitfalls.trapDescription: The classic trap: which is earlier. Goal is the EARLIER target (should); Deadline is the LATER limit (must).
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Goal interval < Deadline interval; urgency increases at each.

examPitfalls.title: What Urgency does
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Urgency is a priority value that rises at goal and deadline — it doesn't move the Case by itself but raises its ranking.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Higher urgency → higher position in Worklists, helping ensure on-time completion.

examPitfalls.title: Single vs. cascading approval
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Cascading approval = multiple sequential approvers (hierarchy/authority matrix), not just one.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Multiple levels of sign-off (e.g., by amount) → cascading approval; one approver → single approval.

examPitfalls.title: Cross-functional Work Groups
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Work Groups coordinate users and Work Queues; cross-functional ones span teams to improve efficiency.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Need members from multiple teams on the same work → cross-functional Work Group.

examPitfalls.title: Routing destination choice
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Scenarios test whether to route to a user or a queue, and whether to use business logic (skill-based).
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Specific owner → user; shared pool → Work Queue; best-available by skill/availability → business-logic routing.

examPitfalls.title: App Studio vs Dev Studio SLA scope
examPitfalls.trapDescription: App Studio offers goal/deadline; advanced SLA options live in Dev Studio.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: BA sets goal/deadline in App Studio; SAs configure advanced escalations/business-day handling in Dev Studio (the SLA rule).

practiceQuiz.scenario: An Assignment must be available to any qualified member of the claims team so whoever is free can pick it up. Where should it be routed?

options.text: To a Work Queue (shared team queue)
To a specific user's Worklist
To the customer
To an Access Role

practiceQuiz.hint: A Work Queue is a shared pool where any qualified team member can pull and complete Assignments.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A Work Queue is the shared queue any qualified team member can work. A Worklist is for a single specific user; the other options are not routing destinations.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which statement correctly distinguishes a goal from a deadline in an SLA?

options.text: The goal is the earlier target time work should be done; the deadline is the later time work must be done
The deadline is earlier than the goal
Goal and deadline are the same time
The goal is mandatory and the deadline is optional

practiceQuiz.hint: The Goal is the earlier 'should-complete-by' target; the Deadline is the later mandatory limit.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The goal is the earlier 'should complete by' target; the deadline is the later 'must complete by' limit. The goal interval is shorter than the deadline interval.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA is configuring SLAs for a high-priority Case Type and needs to explain how Urgency interacts with the goal and deadline milestones. What is the role of Case Urgency relative to deadlines?

options.text: It is a priority value that increases at the goal and again at the deadline, raising the Assignment's ranking in Worklists
It deletes the Case when the deadline passes
It reassigns the Case to the customer
It locks the Ruleset

practiceQuiz.hint: Urgency is a numeric value that increases over time to raise an Assignment's priority in Worklists.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Urgency is a numeric priority that rises at the goal and the deadline, helping at-risk work surface higher in Worklists so it gets done on time.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Expense approvals must be signed off by the submitter's manager and then a director for larger amounts. Which approval pattern is this?

options.text: Cascading approval (multiple sequential approvers via hierarchy/authority matrix)
Single approval
A Work Queue
A duplicate Case search

practiceQuiz.hint: Cascading approval routes through multiple sequential approvers, often based on authority level.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Multiple sequential approvers based on hierarchy or approval amount is cascading approval. A single approval involves only one approver; the other options are unrelated Case features and not approval patterns.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A task must be owned and completed by one specific operator. Where is it routed?

options.text: To that user's Worklist
To a shared Work Queue
To every user in the application
To the Resolution Stage

practiceQuiz.hint: Routing to a named user places the Assignment directly on that operator's personal Worklist.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Routing to a specific user places the Assignment on that user's personal Worklist. A Work Queue is a shared pool for teams; the other routing options (current user, Work Queue) are the only alternatives — not individual role names.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An application needs Assignments routed to whichever qualified agent has the right skill and is available. Which routing approach fits?

options.text: Route using business logic (e.g., skill/availability) to the best-available user
Always route to the current user
Route to the customer
Disable routing entirely

practiceQuiz.hint: Skill-based routing assigns work to the best-available operator based on defined skills or attributes.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Business-logic routing selects the best-available user by criteria such as skill and availability. Routing to the current user ignores skill matching; the others aren't valid.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA is presenting the Work Group concept to a business stakeholder who manages operations across multiple teams. Which TWO statements about Work Groups are correct?

options.text: A Work Group associates users and Work Queues to coordinate work
Cross-functional Work Groups span multiple teams to improve efficiency
A Work Group is the same thing as an Access Role
Work Groups can only contain a single user

practiceQuiz.hint: Work Groups organize users and Work Queues together, and they can span multiple teams or functions.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Work Groups associate users and Work Queues, and cross-functional Work Groups span teams. They are not Access Roles and are not limited to one user. No partial credit.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA configures a goal of 2 hours and a deadline of 8 hours on an Assignment. What happens as time passes?

options.text: Urgency increases when the 2-hour goal is reached and again when the 8-hour deadline is reached
The Case is auto-resolved at 2 hours
The deadline is ignored because the goal is shorter
Nothing changes until 24 hours pass

practiceQuiz.hint: The SLA Goal and Deadline thresholds trigger Urgency increases that escalate overdue Assignments.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Urgency rises at the goal (2h) and again at the deadline (8h), pushing the work up the Worklist. The goal being shorter than the deadline is by design.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Where does a BA set the basic goal and deadline, and where are advanced SLA escalations configured?

options.text: Goal/deadline in App Studio; advanced escalations in Dev Studio (the SLA rule)
Both only in Prediction Studio
Both only in Admin Studio
Neither is configurable

practiceQuiz.hint: Basic in App Studio; advanced in Dev Studio.
practiceQuiz.rationale: BAs set the goal/deadline in App Studio; SAs configure advanced SLA behavior (initial urgency, business days, extra escalations) in Dev Studio on the SLA rule.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In Dev Studio terminology, what is the App Studio 'goal and deadline' called?

options.text: A Service-Level Agreement (SLA)
A Property
An Operator
A Work Group

practiceQuiz.hint: In App Studio the pair of Goal and Deadline is what Dev Studio calls a Service Level Agreement (SLA).
practiceQuiz.rationale: Goal and deadline in App Studio correspond to the Service-Level Agreement (SLA) rule in Dev Studio. The others map to Field, User, and Team respectively.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA has configured an Approve/Reject Step in a loan approval workflow. The approver selects Reject on a submitted application. What typically happens to the Case next?

options.text: It branches off the primary path to rework or rejection handling, based on the reject outcome
It is permanently deleted
It is routed to the customer's Worklist
Nothing changes; approve and reject behave identically

practiceQuiz.hint: An approval step has two distinct outcome paths: approve routes one way, reject routes another.
practiceQuiz.rationale: An approval Step's approve and reject outcomes route the Case down different paths; rejection typically branches to rework or a rejection-handling Stage. Approve and reject are always distinct outcomes that lead to different paths.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO are valid reasons to route an Assignment to a Work Queue rather than a specific user?

options.text: Any qualified member of the team can perform the work
Work should be pulled by whoever becomes available next
Only one named person is allowed to ever do it
The work must be hidden from the entire team

practiceQuiz.hint: A Work Queue is the shared, pull-based construct for team-based Assignment routing.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Work Queues suit shared, pull-based work any qualified member can take. A single mandatory owner indicates a Worklist, and hiding work from the team is not a routing goal. No partial credit.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the primary business value of assignment routing and approvals as workflow-automation features?

options.text: They orchestrate work across teams and ensure the right people complete the right work efficiently and on time
They eliminate the need for any users
They replace the Case Life Cycle
They store data in external systems

practiceQuiz.hint: Routing and approvals ensure the right work reaches the right person at the right time.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Routing and approvals orchestrate cross-team work by getting the right Assignments to the right operators efficiently and supporting on-time, governed completion. They are foundational to structured business process management.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA is explaining to a business user how a single Approve/Reject Step affects Case routing in a workflow. Which option best describes how a single approval step interacts with the Case flow?

options.text: One approver decides approve/reject, and the outcome routes the Case forward or to rework
Every user in the org must approve before proceeding
Approvals never affect the Case path
Approvals are only decorative

practiceQuiz.hint: A single approval involves exactly one approver whose decision (approve/reject) determines the next path.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A single approval has one approver whose approve or reject decision routes the Case to the appropriate next path. Requiring everyone to approve describes a different pattern; single approval is about one decision-maker.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Why might a BA choose a Worklist over a Work Queue for a sensitive compliance review?

options.text: Because a specific, accountable individual must own and complete the review
Because no one should ever see it
Because Work Queues cannot hold Assignments
Because Worklists are faster to delete

practiceQuiz.hint: Assigning work to a specific named user creates direct accountability with one designated owner.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A Worklist assigns work to a specific accountable owner, appropriate when one named individual must complete a sensitive task. Work Queues can hold Assignments (shared); the other options are false.

quickRecap.value: Send Assignments to the best-available user. Worklist = specific user; Work Queue = shared team queue; business-logic routing = by skill/availability.
Associate users and Work Queues; cross-functional Work Groups span teams to improve efficiency. (Team in App Studio = Work Group in Dev Studio.)
Single (one approver) vs. cascading (multiple sequential approvers via hierarchy/authority matrix); approve/reject routes the Case.
Goal = earlier 'should-by' target; deadline = later 'must-by' limit; goal interval < deadline interval.
Numeric priority that increases at the goal and again at the deadline, raising Worklist ranking to drive on-time completion.
BA sets goal/deadline in App Studio; SAs configure advanced SLA escalations/business-day handling in Dev Studio.
